problem:
$$
B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]},\,C={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -6\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 19\end{aligned}]},\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

 

The bases $B$ and $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B$ are given above. Find $[x]_{C}.$
worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ and $C$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ and ${{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$, respectively.

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ is a matrix whose columns are the vectors of $B$ relative to the basis $C.$

Hence, we need to find the coordinates of ${b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2}$ relative to the basis $C.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} & {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we simply reduce the left-hand side to reduced row-echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 & 1 \\ -6 & 19 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+6{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 7 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 22 & 19 \\ 0 & 1 & 7 & 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{B\to C}$ is

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}22 & 19 \\ 7 & 6\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we compute $[\,x\,]_{C}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{C} & ={P}_{B\to C}[\,x\,]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}22 & 19 \\ 7 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
